I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life, and my father before me. I know what grows here and what does not. The land is flat, the water is deep underground but I can pump it. The winters are cold and dry, the summers are hot and wet enough for corn.

I will grow wheat and corn, same as always. Wheat goes in the ground in October after I harvest the corn. Corn goes in after wheat harvest in June. This is what every farmer here does. My neighbors do it, my father did it. I see no reason to change.

For seeds I will go to the township seed shop and buy what they have. For wheat they usually have Kenong 199 or Jimai 22 — improved varieties. The shop owner says these give good yields. For corn I have been using Zhengdan 958 for years, it is a hybrid and I know how it behaves on my fields.

For fertilizer I put down a base application before planting, then top-dress in spring for wheat and at the jointing stage for corn. My son told me some people are using less fertilizer but I do not want to risk a poor harvest. I will apply what I have always applied.

I irrigate wheat four times — once at sowing to help germination, once before winter freeze, once at jointing, once at heading. For corn I irrigate maybe twice if there is no rain.

I have 10 mu total. I keep 8 mu for wheat and corn rotation. The other 2 mu near the house I plant with garlic and vegetables for my family and to sell a little at the village market in spring.

I plough and rotary-till before wheat planting. For summer corn I just seed directly into the wheat stubble, no deep tillage. This saves me time and fuel.
